rule: guide/print/orientation-study/PRINT-ORIENTATION-PRACTICE.md step 2 (flagged part: slice the best-screened alternative) and R2/R6; coordinator rule: a pose whose supports land on a functional mating face loses, otherwise lower support-on-model area, then lower height

method.contactRule: support extrusion samples within 0.8 mm of the part surface (0.25 mm even surface sampling); landing = touched faces with |print nz| > 0.5, adjacent = vertical faces

current.pose: bottom wall (robot z -44) on the bed; release pose, back-plate/rear_frame-print.stl
current.supportOnLipFaces: lip underside (source normal -z, z 27.3, 198.0 mm2): faces the cable channel, mates with nothing (wires clear it by 0.4 mm per back-plate/README.md). Lip sides and front only adjacent (vertical, 0.35 mm XY gap).

sidewall.pose: orientation-check 'stable p=0.08': +y side wall on the bed (x' = z, y' = -x, z' = -y)
sidewall.supportOnLipFaces: lip +y side face (source normal +y, y 13.2, 9.0 mm2, facing down in this pose): one of the two faces that locate the frame between the pack side walls with 0.4 mm per side.

decision: KEEP bottom-down (current release pose). The side-wall pose puts support on the lip +y locating side (9.0 mm2), a functional mating face, so it loses by the first rule. Bottom-down lands support on no mating face: the lip underside it supports faces the cable channel. It also has the lower support-on-model area (3384.8 against 4012.5 mm2; the side pose adds 910.1 mm2 of support bases on up-facing inner faces). The side pose is lower (64.1 against 90.5 mm), steadier (tip 10.5 against 8.3 deg) and 0.97 g lighter in support, at the same time (4953 against 4927 s). No change to rows.json, the manifest or any release file; the 4 mm brim stays for the 8.3 deg tip angle.
limits: Contact measured from toolpath proximity, not a print; touched area counts whole triangles. Bambu only.
